full_details: At St Helen's the almanac stayed on your knee and you made no mark in it. At dinner the loaf was a penny and a full thumb short of the notch, and you took the soft side. Your jaw was quiet, the first Sunday it had been so since August. In the evening Alse cut an arm's length of red thread on her own arm. You faired what you have of the lovers, left the rehearsal marks in the margins, and did not write finished on the first leaf. The dawn in the bundle is the one already written. You laid the bundle apart from the private verse, your hand flat on it, and wrote the three lines home before you corrected another word. Gib sat on the Holinshed.
one_sentence: You ate the soft side of a short loaf, tied the fair copy in red thread, and wrote Anne three lines before another correction.
title: A quiet jaw, a red thread, three lines
